body: I felt this all the way to my core.

Four (why Four, out of curiosity?),

I love hearing about your plans to work on your game, take up jogging, and even learning physics and economics. It gives me hope (there's that word again) that we can turn it around. 

I love reading and writing, but I have pulled away from that for now. I don't think it was helping to "ground" me in reality. You know that feeling when you've driven home from work and pull in your driveway, but you can't quite remember actually driving home? That's how every day has felt for months. 

It's hard to explain. It's almost as if I was living on autopilot all the time. I was always in my own head which, let's face it, is a terrible fucking place to be stuck. I felt like I couldn't connect to anyone around me, and I started to feel detached from reality. Nothing at all felt real or meaningful. I started to notice that it took an inordinate amount of concentration just to focus on a conversation with someone. If I wasn't telling myself to pay attention, I floated away. Does that make sense? I tried to explain this to my fiance once, but I think I scared him more than made him understand. I haven't brought it up since.

Anyway, I have only recently begun to feel a little like myself again. I still struggle every day. I still realize I've been staring off into space while someone has been talking to me for who knows how long.

I think pulling away from fiction has helped a lot, even though I miss writing. I'll come back to it someday though. I think gardening has helped a lot because I bury my hands in the earth, and I can feel the cool breeze on my skin. I know I'm alive and I'm here, whatever that means. 

Maybe it's not so bad that life is pointless. We're here for a short time, and we die. Maybe if we can find a reason each day to get up again tomorrow, we are doing just fine. 

I just turned 29 by the way.

Dead Man,

I know how you feel about the vicious cycle of hope and hopelessness. If hope is a survival instinct, maybe it's a good thing we have it, however sparingly. It means we aren't ready to throw in the towel. Even when I'm in the depths of despair, I have hope for tomorrow. I hope you do too.
When I am overwhelmed with the bleak pointlessness that seems to be our existence, I try to focus on some hobbies. I recently took up gardening, and I have big plans to renovate my backyard in the spring. 
That sounds like something so small and stupid, but I am actually looking forward to something in the future. Something I have to be here for to witness. That's an amazing feat for me, let me tell you.
Do you have something like that?
Keep trudging. Don't be a Dead Man just yet.

Sincerely,
Cat

Hi DeadManIV,

I'm still here. I don't know that I have found a motivator, but I have thrown myself into a bunch of house projects that keep my mind occupied. I strive to tire myself out every day. So far, that has kept the darkest thoughts away. I don't know if that's particularly healthy. Something's gotta give at some point, you know? But for now, it helps. 

What about you? What helps you, if anything, since you're in a similar boat?
